chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
At the extremity of hardship comes relief, and at the tightening of the chains of tribulation comes ease.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between extreme hardship and relief in Shia teachings?
ai.summary: In this maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) articulates the dialectic of divine decree, reflecting the Shia understanding that peak intensity in tribulation signals the imminent arrival of relief. This principle serves as both a theological comfort and a practical guide for patience (sabr), reminding believers that the tightening of a trial's 'throat' is the precursor to divine expansion (faraaj).

en.sayed-ali-raza: 351. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
At the extremity of hardship comes relief, and at the tightening of the chains of tribulation comes ease.
